conclusions.finding: Checkpoint-25 I/N readouts had 24 rows each, field enabled, zero distribution/landing/pressure/payload, and identical paired outputs.

Across persisted developmental traces, 1,526/1,600 rows had a trace; 1,463 rows had nonzero distributions/landings/pressure/payload after excluding persisted zero rows; 74 rows lacked a separate trace.
No introspection adjustment was accepted: 100 reviews, 75 malformed, 4 no-targets, 21 no-change, zero accessibility/expression adjustments.

I/N divergence is attributable to SAA payload/landing and subsequent adaptive graph/learner feedback rather than introspection; direct paired traces show differing payloads and outputs from the same query/seed, while checkpoint graph digests and counts diverge.

The compact evidence cannot establish the exact cause of every missing late field trace (T075/T087/T089/T095/T096/T100), nor whether every no-change review was a genuine semantic no-change rather than an unrecorded empty proposal.

The SAA lottery operated on most accepted developmental coordinates with candidate distributions, seeded landings, local pressure and rendered payloads; the evidence is insufficient to establish a clean familiar-versus-novel flattening causal relationship because novelty/context distributions and missing-trace intervals are confounded.
P3 provides no interpretable evidence for an introspection effect: accepted introspection treatment was zero. I/N divergence cannot be attributed to introspection.
